sbh2.0:3.5: The person by whom, in previous other births, hatred was resorted to, cultivated, [and] made much of —

sbh2.0:3.11: by that cause, by that condition,
sbh2.0:3.12: [he] now has intense delusion and prolonged delusion toward an object of delusion. This is called the delusion-intoxicated person.
sbh2.0:3.14: The person by whom, in previous other births, conceit was resorted to, cultivated, [and] made much of — by that cause, by that condition,
sbh2.0:3.15: [he] now has intense conceit and prolonged conceit toward a conceit-arousing object.
sbh2.0:4.1: This is called the conceit-intoxicated person.
sbh2.0:4.3: The person by whom, in previous other births, applied thought was resorted to, cultivated, [and] made much of — by that cause, by that condition, [he] now has intense applied-thought and prolonged applied-thought toward an object that is the place of applied thought.
sbh2.0:5.2: The person by whom, in previous other births, lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, [and] applied-thought were not resorted to, cultivated, [or] made much of, and [for whom] these dharmas were not seen as dangerous,
sbh2.0:5.4: he, by that cause, by that condition, in a lust-arousing or hate-arousing or conceit-arousing or applied-thought-arousing object, does not have intense lust,
sbh2.0:5.6: and lust does not become manifest in him from that object.
sbh2.0:5.7: As with lust, so with hatred, delusion, conceit, [and] applied-thought.
sbh2.0:5.8: This is called the balanced-attaining person.
sbh2.0:5.10: The person by whom, in previous other births, lust was not resorted to, [not] made much of,
sbh2.0:5.11: and [who] has often seen it as dangerous,
sbh2.0:5.13: he, by that cause, by that condition, now [only] toward a lust-arousing object [that is] present, manifest, strong, abundant, [and] glaring, produces lust [matching] that [great] lust[-arousing thing];
sbh2.0:5.14: toward a middle or small one, he does not produce [it].
sbh2.0:5.15: As with lust, so with hatred, delusion, conceit, [and] applied-thought are to be understood.
sbh2.0:5.16: This is called the slight-dust person.

sbh2.0:13.2: This person, by the abandonment of the three fetters — personality-view [satkāya-dṛṣṭi], clinging-to-virtue-and-vow [śīlavrata-parāmarśa], [and] doubt [vicikitsā] — becomes a stream-enterer,

sbh2.0:13.6: Both stream-enterer persons [the seven-times-at-most and the family-to-family] are to be understood [so].
sbh2.0:13.7: Now, what is the one-gap person [ekabījin]?
sbh2.0:13.8: For this practitioner of the once-returner [and] non-returner fruit, the strong and middle realm-of-desire defilements are abandoned,
sbh2.0:13.10: and, having produced only one realm-of-desire existence, there itself he attains final nirvāṇa.
sbh2.0:13.11: He once returns to this [world] — this is called the one-gap [one].
sbh2.0:14.5: just upon decease, at the time of intermediate-existence-generation, [he] generates the intermediate existence and at the very moment of generation attains final nirvāṇa —

sbh2.0:20.1: What is the delineation of persons?
sbh2.0:20.2: The delineation of persons is to be understood by eleven divisions.
sbh2.0:20.3: By which eleven? Namely: by division of faculty, by division of sect, by division of conduct, by division of vow, [by division of practice,] by division of path-fruit, by division of application,
sbh2.0:20.4: by division of attainment, by division of rebirth, by division of falling-back, [and] by division of obscuration.
sbh2.0:21.2: [there is] the delineation of mild-faculty and sharp-faculty persons.
sbh2.0:22.1: By division of sect [pārṣadya], the delineation of seven kinds of person:
sbh2.0:22.2: monk, nun, female probationer, male novice, female novice, layman, laywoman.
sbh2.0:23.1: Now, by division of conduct, the delineation of seven persons:
sbh2.0:23.2: he who is the lust-intoxicated person is lust-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.3: he who is hatred-intoxicated is hatred-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.4: he who is delusion-intoxicated is delusion-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.5: he who is conceit-intoxicated is conceit-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.6: he who is applied-thought-intoxicated is applied-thought-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.7: he who is balanced-attaining is balanced-conducted;
sbh2.0:23.8: he who is slight-dust is slight-conducted — [thus they are] to be understood.
sbh2.0:24.1: Now, what are the marks of the lust-conducted person?
sbh2.0:24.2: Here the lust-conducted person, [even] toward a slight, wholly inferior lust-arousing object, produces a dense, strong lust-obsession —
sbh2.0:24.3: what more toward a middle or fine [object]?
sbh2.0:24.4: And that lust-obsession he maintains in continuity for a long time,
sbh2.0:24.5: [remains] bound [by it] for a long time.
sbh2.0:24.6: Through that obsession, he is overcome by lust-arousing dharmas,
sbh2.0:24.7: but he is not able to overcome the lust-arousing dharmas.
sbh2.0:24.8: He is of smooth faculties, of non-harsh faculties,
sbh2.0:24.9: not of harsh faculties, not of cut-off faculties;
sbh2.0:24.10: not too much harming others — namely by body or by speech; [yet he is] hard to instruct, hard to admonish;
sbh2.0:24.16: great in [his demand for] requisites and provisions, of greedy nature, taking that [demand] as guru[-like authority]; full of joy, full of delight, free from frowning, of open-faced complexion, accompanied by a smile. — What are the marks of the hatred-conducted person?
sbh2.0:24.18: toward a hateful object, [even] by a slight resistance-cause-sign, produces a dense, abundant resistance-obsession —
sbh2.0:24.19: what more by a middle or strong [one]?
sbh2.0:24.20: And that resistance-obsession he maintains in continuity for a long time,
sbh2.0:24.21: [remains] bound [by it] for a long time.
sbh2.0:24.23: he is overcome by hateful dharmas,
sbh2.0:24.24: but cannot overcome the hateful dharmas.
sbh2.0:24.26: of harsh faculties, of cut-off faculties, of fierce faculties, and is excessively harming others by nature —
sbh2.0:24.27: namely by body and by speech.
sbh2.0:24.28: Yet he is easy to advise,
sbh2.0:24.32: not of firm action, not of stable action;
sbh2.0:24.33: not of firm vow, not of stable vow;
sbh2.0:24.34: full of dejection, full of distress;
sbh2.0:24.37: a non-respectful-grasper, of hard-to-bring-back nature, full of grudges;
sbh2.0:24.38: of cruel hopes, fierce, of straight-grasping speech, of present-tense speech — even when slightly addressed, he is offended,
sbh2.0:24.44: of non-open face, hating others’ fortune, full of envy. — Such kinds of marks of the hatred-conducted person are to be understood.
sbh2.0:25.1: Now, what are the marks of the delusion-conducted person?
sbh2.0:25.2: Here the delusion-conducted person, [even] toward a slight delusion-arousing object, produces a dense, abundant delusion-obsession —
sbh2.0:25.3: [and] still more toward a middle or strong [object]; and he maintains the continuity of that delusion-obsession for a long time,
sbh2.0:25.5: He is overcome by delusion-arousing dharmas,
sbh2.0:25.6: but cannot overcome the delusion-arousing dharmas.
sbh2.0:25.9: of intoxicated faculties, of loose bodily action; an ill-thought-thinker, ill-speech-speaker, ill-deed-doer; lazy, not endowed with [the capacity for] rising;
sbh2.0:25.13: a wrong-grasper, hard to advise, hard to admonish, of inferior conviction;
sbh2.0:25.16: to understand the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken [teachings], and of other-following nature,
sbh2.0:25.17: other-led, other-guided. — Such kinds of marks of the delusion-conducted person are to be understood.
sbh2.0:26.1: Now, what are the marks of the conceit-conducted person?
sbh2.0:26.2: Here the conceit-conducted person, [even] toward a slight conceit-arousing object, produces a dense conceit-obsession —
sbh2.0:26.3: what more toward a middle or strong [one]?
sbh2.0:26.4: And the continuity of that conceit-obsession he maintains for a long time,
sbh2.0:26.6: [Repeating:] What are the marks of the conceit-conducted person?
sbh2.0:26.7: Here the conceit-conducted person, [even] toward a slight conceit-arousing object, produces a dense conceit-obsession — what more toward a middle or strong [one]?
sbh2.0:26.8: The continuity of that conceit-obsession he maintains for a long time,
sbh2.0:26.9: and is bound by it; he is overcome by conceit-place dharmas,
sbh2.0:26.10: but cannot overcome the conceit-place dharmas.
sbh2.0:26.11: He is of restless faculties, of arrogant faculties, of high faculties; engaged in adorning the body, he speaks an excessively haughty speech, not lowered [in tone]; and toward those who should be respected — those suffering, the gurus, persons occupying the place of guru — from time to time he is not a doer of the proper respect.
sbh2.0:26.13: of non-humble body, not respectful in salutation, bowing, [or] rising; not skilled in the proper service; self-grasping, self-exalting, other-deprecating;
sbh2.0:26.14: desirous of gain, desirous of honor, desirous of fame, voice, [and] eulogy;
sbh2.0:26.16: hard to advise, of grand conviction,
sbh2.0:26.18: and full of strong views of self, being, soul, person, [and] individual, with anger,
sbh2.0:26.19: full of grudges. — Now, what are the marks of the applied-thought-conducted person?
sbh2.0:26.20: Here the applied-thought-conducted person, [even] toward a slight applied-thought-place object, produces a dense obsession,
sbh2.0:26.21: and that obsession he maintains for a long time,
sbh2.0:26.23: He is overcome by applied-thought-place dharmas,
sbh2.0:26.24: but cannot overcome the applied-thought-place dharmas.
sbh2.0:26.30: of corrupt verbal action; hard to instruct, hard to admonish; fond of [conceptual] proliferation [prapañca], delighting in proliferation;
sbh2.0:26.31: full of doubt, full of indecision;
sbh2.0:26.32: and of varied desire, of unstable vow,
sbh2.0:26.36: full of suspicion, of stolen mindfulness;
sbh2.0:26.37: non-delighting in seclusion, full of distraction;
sbh2.0:26.39: [though sometimes] skilful, [yet] non-lazy [only in distractions]. — Such kinds of marks of the applied-thought-conducted person are to be understood.
sbh2.0:27.1: This is the delineation of persons by division of conduct, [thus] to be understood.
sbh2.0:28.1: Now, the delineation of persons by division of vow [praṇidhāna]:
sbh2.0:28.2: there is a person who has made his vow in the disciple-vehicle,
sbh2.0:28.3: there is one in the solitary-buddha-vehicle,
sbh2.0:28.4: [and] there is one in the great vehicle.
sbh2.0:28.6: who has made his vow in the disciple-vehicle may be of disciple-lineage, may be of solitary-buddha-lineage,
sbh2.0:28.8: [Likewise,] this person who has made his vow in [the path of] solitary awakening may also be of solitary-buddha-lineage, of disciple-lineage, [or] of great-vehicle-lineage.
sbh2.0:28.9: [And] this person who has made his vow in the great vehicle may also be of disciple-lineage, may be of solitary-buddha-lineage, [or] may be of great-vehicle-lineage.
sbh2.0:28.10: [Now,] this disciple-lineage person who has made his vow in solitary awakening or in supreme perfect awakening —
sbh2.0:28.11: he, on account of his disciple-lineage, necessarily at the final time will turn back that vow and stand only in the disciple-vehicle vow.
sbh2.0:28.12: Thus the solitary-buddha-lineage and great-vehicle-lineage [persons] are to be understood.
sbh2.0:28.13: There is, for these persons, a requisite of vow [and] a transmission of vow [from one life to the next],
sbh2.0:28.14: but not a requisite of lineage [or] a transmission of lineage.
sbh2.0:28.15: In this [śrāvakabhūmi] context, these persons are to be understood as of disciple-vehicle vow and of disciple-lineage.
sbh2.0:29.1: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of vow.
sbh2.0:30.1: How is the delineation of persons by division of practice [pratipatti]?
sbh2.0:30.2: Of these persons just pointed out [and] proclaimed, [their] going forth is by four practices.
sbh2.0:30.4: There is the painful practice with slow knowledge [duḥkhā pratipad dhandhābhijñā];
sbh2.0:30.5: there is the painful practice with quick knowledge [duḥkhā pratipad kṣiprābhijñā];
sbh2.0:30.6: there is the pleasant practice with slow knowledge [sukhā pratipad dhandhābhijñā]; [and] there is the pleasant practice with quick knowledge [sukhā pratipad kṣiprābhijñā].
sbh2.0:31.1: Of the mild-faculty person, [who is] a gainer of [only the] preliminary dhyāna [anāgamya], the practice is called painful, with slow knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.2: Of the sharp-faculty person, [who is] a gainer of [only the] preliminary dhyāna, the practice is called painful, with quick knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.3: Of the mild-faculty person, [who is] a gainer of the [full] basic dhyāna [maula-dhyāna], the practice is called pleasant, with slow knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.4: Of the sharp-faculty person, [who is] a gainer of the [full] basic dhyāna, the practice is called pleasant, with quick knowledge.
sbh2.0:31.5: Thus the delineation of persons by division of practice is to be understood.
sbh2.0:32.1: Now, how is the delineation of persons by division of path-fruit to be understood?
sbh2.0:32.3: of the four practitioners — practitioner for the fruit of stream-entry, of once-returning, of non-returning, [and] of arhatship — and of the four fruit-attainers — stream-enterer, once-returner,
sbh2.0:32.4: non-returner, [and] arhat — and of those for whom the practitioner-paths [still] proceed:
sbh2.0:32.5: they are practitioners; their delineation is by the practitioner-path.
sbh2.0:32.6: [Those] established in the arhat-fruit [and the lesser] recluse-fruits — their delineation is the path-fruit delineation. Thus is the delineation of persons by division of path-fruit.
sbh2.0:33.1: How is the delineation of persons by division of application?
sbh2.0:33.2: Namely, by [the categories of] faith-follower and dharma-follower.
sbh2.0:33.3: The person who is applied [to the path] by faith-following
sbh2.0:33.4: is the faith-follower; the one applied in [the] dharmas by following the discipline derived from another’s conditions [i.e., received instruction] is the dharma-follower.
sbh2.0:33.5: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of application.
sbh2.0:33.6: Now, how is the delineation of persons by division of attainment [samāpatti]?
sbh2.0:33.7: Namely, of the body-witness: the witness, having realized the eight liberations with the body, dwells having attained [them],
sbh2.0:33.8: and does not entirely attain the destruction of the fluxes.
sbh2.0:33.10: Inwardly with non-form perception, [yet] externally he sees forms [second vimokṣa].
sbh2.0:33.11: He realizes the pure liberation with the body and dwells having attained [third vimokṣa].
sbh2.0:33.12: The sphere of infinity of space, infinity of consciousness, nothingness, neither-perception-nor-non-perception, [and] the cessation of perception-and-feeling [fourth through eighth vimokṣa], in forward and reverse order he attains and rises out [of].
sbh2.0:33.13: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of attainment.
sbh2.0:33.14: How is the delineation of persons by division of rebirth?
sbh2.0:33.16: Namely, [the delineation] of the seven-times-at-most, of the family-to-family, of the one-gap, of the in-between-nirvāṇa, of the upon-rebirth-nirvāṇa, [and] of the upstream-goer.
sbh2.0:33.17: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of rebirth.
sbh2.0:33.18: How is the delineation of persons by division of falling-back?
sbh2.0:33.20: Namely, of the sometimes-liberated arhat, who is liable to falling back from the seen-dharma pleasure-dwellings, the delineation [is made] by the division of falling-back, [and conversely for the unshakable];
sbh2.0:34.1: of the unshakable-dharma arhat, who is not liable to falling back from the seen-dharma pleasure-dwellings, [the delineation is made by the division of non-falling-back].
sbh2.0:34.2: Thus is the delineation of persons by division of falling-back.
sbh2.0:34.3: Now, how is the delineation of persons by division of obscuration [āvaraṇa]?

sbh2.0:104.161: Likewise others, seeing one seated in this posture, are exceedingly cleared in mind; this posture is resorted to and authorized by the Buddhas and the Buddha-disciples.
sbh2.0:104.164: Folding the legs, having set the body upright.
sbh2.0:104.166: The body being clearly raised and held straight.
sbh2.0:104.167: Not by careless mind, but by uprightness free of pretense.
sbh2.0:104.168: There, with body upright, taken hold of, sloth-and-torpor of mind does not overwhelm and stand.
sbh2.0:104.169: Without pretense, outward distraction of mind does not overwhelm and stand.
sbh2.0:104.172: The mindfulness which he establishes, associated with wise attention, is called ‘fronting before,’
sbh2.0:104.173: by way of being-in-front-of all the dark side and going-counter-to it.
sbh2.0:104.174: Further, mindfulness whose object is the concentration-sign, an object that is a likeness, is called ‘fronting before,’
sbh2.0:104.175: by way of being-in-front-of all the concentration-plane object. This is called fullness of posture.
sbh2.0:104.180: There, bodily withdrawal: not dwelling together with householders or renunciants.
sbh2.0:105.1: There, mental withdrawal: avoiding defiled and indeterminate mental engagement,
sbh2.0:105.2: he cultivates a mental engagement belonging to the concentration-plane or preparatory for the requisites of concentration.
sbh2.0:105.3: Wholesome, connected with the meaning — this is called mental withdrawal.
sbh2.0:105.4: There, the fullness of place, this fullness of posture,
sbh2.0:105.6: this mental withdrawal — these gathered into one are called ‘seclusion.’
sbh2.0:105.9: the recurrent mindfulness-with-conformable-object, mental continuity yoked to unobjectionable delight in flow,
sbh2.0:105.10: that mental continuum is called concentration.
sbh2.0:105.12: What does he recollect again and again?
sbh2.0:105.14: the dharmas grasped, heard, and the admonition-instruction received.
sbh2.0:105.15: Making the instruction from teachers predominant, bringing forth the sign pertaining to the concentration-plane, he follows up mindfulness yoked to its flow with that as object.
sbh2.0:105.20: by which the mind is supremely concentrated on the object, this is called
sbh2.0:105.25: it is a likeness of the thing-of-destruction. Therefore it is called conformable.
sbh2.0:105.26: And that unbroken, gap-less, uninterrupted mindfulness which proceeds,
sbh2.0:105.27: in flow yoked, continually and with respect, by that object,
sbh2.0:105.28: in delight in that very object, dwelling undefiled,
sbh2.0:105.29: borne on the path mindfulness — this is the delight-flow-yoked-quality.
sbh2.0:105.30: Hence: ‘again and again with-conformable-object, flow yoked to unobjectionable delight, mental continuum,’
sbh2.0:105.31: is concentration. Such, indeed, is it.
